title: Recording: Long Haired Lady, Sunshine Sometime by Paul and Linda McCartney | 1970
content:
Studio B, CBS Studio Building, New York City
Producers: Paul McCartney, Linda McCartney

Paul McCartney worked on two songs on 29 October 1970: ‘Long Haired Lady’ for the Ram album, and the session outtake ‘Sunshine Sometime’.

He had begun work on ‘Long Haired Lady’ two days before, but more work was needed on the arrangement.

The backing track was completed on this day, with McCartney on his Martin D-28 acoustic guitar and guide vocals, Hugh McCracken on his Gibson ES-335 electric guitar, and Denny Seiwell on drums.

They then switched their attention to ‘Sunshine Sometime’, which McCartney had earmarked for his mooted Rupert The Bear animated feature film. At this point the song had the working title ‘Sunshine Sometimes’.

I kind of remember using some African drums an clicking on the rims with a wooden stick… we built that track as we went, but basic was done with everyone playing at the same time and then a few overdubs to complete it.
Denny Seiwell
Maccazine, October 2012

‘Sunshine Sometime’ was officially released on the 2012 reissue of Ram.

Overdubs were added, probably in July 1978, including Paul and Linda McCartney’s and Paul’s bass guitar part. That version remains unreleased.

Page last updated: 8 November 2025
